Log-structured merge trees explained

A log-structured merge tree buffers writes in memory and flushes them to sorted files on disk.

Every write is first recorded in a write-ahead log so that the memory buffer survives a crash.

Background compaction merges sorted files and discards overwritten values.

RocksDB and LevelDB are widely used storage engines built on LSM trees.
